_about: Yinyue's past as the game gives it back (doc/drafts/yinyue-backstory.md, approved). One entry per chapter: the memory its cauldron returns (`memory` — her own line, or `scene`, the spine scene that already says it), what she now knows (`knows`) and how she carries it (`feels`). The rules hand over only what the chapters ENDED have returned, and only once she walks with the player (companion.mjs § 她的来处). `secret` is realized at `realized`, kept, and told once `told` has ended; `whole` resolves it. `fear` is handed to her from the day she joins; `want` is never handed to anyone — it is what the last beat of the story answers, never something she asks for.

fear.zh: 被放在某处等。两千年她很会等了——等得很好，不想再练。
fear.en: Being set down somewhere to wait. Two thousand years made her good at it — good enough; she does not want the practice.

want.zh: 到了最后，有人问她留不留。不是被放下，是被问。
want.en: At the very end, to be asked whether she will stay. Not set down — asked.

knows.zh: 她不记得自己是谁，只知道那只铃是她的，她等了很久。
knows.en: She does not remember who she was — only that the bell is hers and she waited a long while.

feels.zh: 被找到了，高兴，嘴上不说。
feels.en: Found, and glad of it, though she will not make much of it.

text.zh: 有人把我放进水里，说：等一个会来的人。
text.en: Someone laid me in the water and said: wait for one who comes.

knows.zh: 她是被人放进水里的，不是落水的。
knows.en: She was set down in the water on purpose, not lost in it.

feels.zh: 有些怔：原来她一直在等，而等的人来了。
feels.en: A little stunned: she has been waiting all along, and the one she waited for came.

text.zh: 那只手背上有鼎纹。它数着，一直数到九。
text.en: The hand had a cauldron's pattern on its back. It counted, all the way to nine.

knows.zh: 放她下水的那只手与鼎有关；九。
knows.en: The hand that set her down belongs to the cauldrons somehow; and nine.

feels.zh: 好奇那是谁的手，又有点怕知道。
feels.en: Curious whose hand it was, and a little afraid to know.

knows.zh: 她被放在东海；那人要她等九鼎聚齐，还叫了一个不是她的名字。
knows.en: She was set down in the eastern sea; she was told to wait until the nine are gathered, and a name was spoken that was not hers.

feels.zh: 头一回觉得这条路和她自己有关。
feels.en: For the first time the road feels like it is about her too.

text.zh: 那铃是陪着这口鼎的。我摇过它——我那时有手。
text.en: That bell kept this cauldron company. I rang it — I had hands then.

knows.zh: 铃是她的；她曾是个活生生的铃童，替人摇铃。
knows.en: The bell is hers; she was once a living bell-child who rang it for someone.

feels.zh: 鼎起之后，心里空了一小块，说不上是什么，也不提。
feels.en: Since this cauldron rose, something small in her has gone quiet; she cannot name it and does not mention it.

text.zh: 一张老妇人的脸，手背上有鼎纹。她不是我娘。我没有人，她也没有人，就凑成了两个。
text.en: An old woman's face, a cauldron's pattern on the back of her hand. She was not my mother. I had no one and neither did she, so we made two.

knows.zh: 守鼎的是一位老妇人；她自己无父无母，无姓无族。
knows.en: The keeper of the cauldrons was an old woman; she herself had no parents, no name of a house, no clan.

feels.zh: 又少了点什么；看水的时候更久了，却更爱看你走在前面。
feels.en: A little less again; she looks at water longer now, and likes more than ever to watch you walk ahead.

text.zh: 她教过我一句话：在德不在鼎。鼎的轻重，不可问。
text.en: She taught me one thing: it lies in virtue, not in the cauldron. What a cauldron weighs is not to be asked.

knows.zh: 守鼎人教她的道理：在德不在鼎。
knows.en: The keeper's lesson: it lies in virtue, not in the cauldron.

feels.zh: 怕你成了问鼎的人——又知道你不是。夜里有时找不到自己在水里的影子，不提。
feels.en: Afraid you might become one who asks what cauldrons weigh — and sure you are not. Some nights she cannot find her own reflection in the water; she does not mention it.

text.zh: 她最后叫的是“文命”。她叫的不是我——是一个会走遍九州的人。
text.en: The name she called at the last was Wenming. She was not calling me — she was calling one who would walk all nine provinces.

knows.zh: 文命是禹的名字；那个“会来的人”，是走遍九州的人——是你。
knows.en: Wenming was Yu's name; the one who comes is the one who walks all nine provinces — you.

feels.zh: 看你的时候多了点什么。心里的不安重了，却更不肯让你为她慢下来。
feels.en: Something more when she looks at you. The unease in her is heavier, and she is all the more set that you never slow down for her.

text.zh: 周亡那夜，秦人来搬鼎。她一口一口数着，把九鼎送回九州的水里。守，是我自己要的。
text.en: The night Zhou fell, Qin came for the cauldrons. She counted them out one by one, back into the waters of the nine provinces. Keeping them was my own wish.

knows.zh: 周亡那夜的事；守鼎是她自愿的。她把瞒着的事说出来了。
knows.en: The night Zhou fell; she chose to keep the cauldrons. She has told what she was keeping back.

feels.zh: 说出口了，轻了些。还怕，但不再瞒你。
feels.en: Lighter for having said it. Still afraid, but no longer hiding it from you.

text.zh: 洛水边，月夜，有人从水上捡起一个婴儿，给她起名：银，是她日后要摇的铃；月，是那夜水上的月。
text.en: By the Luo, on a moonlit night, someone lifted a baby off the water and named her: Yin, silver, for the bell she would ring; Yue, the moon, for the moon on the water that night.

knows.zh: 她的来处；九鼎聚齐，九影归一，她还在，是完整的。
knows.en: Where she came from; the nine are gathered, the nine reflections are one, and she is still here — whole.

feels.zh: 完整，安定。留下是她自己选的。
feels.en: Whole and settled. Staying is her own choice.

text.zh: 每起一口鼎，我在那处水上的影子就被收回一个。九鼎聚齐时，再没有一处水盛得住我。我没说，是怕你为我放慢。
text.en: Each cauldron raised takes back my reflection from that water. When the nine are gathered, no water will be left to hold me. I did not say it because I was afraid you would slow down for me.

resolved.zh: 千江有水千江月——天上的月只有一轮，江里的都是影子。原来只有一轮。
resolved.en: A thousand rivers, a thousand moons — yet there is one moon in the sky; the rest are reflections. So there was only ever one.
